A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same minimum-distance summaries (MDS) research. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material reorganized from v1 Appendix D into v2 Appendices D–F.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original simulation experiments on Gaussian, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, SIR and cryo-EM tasks, including posterior accuracy, coverage and contamination robustness.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds optimization and bandwidth sensitivity results, learned-summary OUP evaluation and stronger SIR contamination experiments.

M1.justification: The decoder, random-feature MMD objective and fixed-NPE adaptation remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 adds an optional inference variant that runs ten optimizations from perturbed initial summaries and selects the best resulting MDS; it does not replace the default single-start procedure.

E1.justification: The Gaussian, OUP, SIR and cryo-EM task coverage is retained. Appendix F.3.1 extends SIR testing beyond 50% contamination to fully distorted observations at epsilon = 1, adding a more severe input scenario. Learned-summary OUP is a configuration change within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The retained experiments preserve their NPE, NNPE, NPE-OR, NPE-RS, NPE-PFN and KL-based MDS comparisons. Added experiments reuse existing comparators or subsets of them. Bharti et al. (2026) is newly discussed but not evaluated; NNPE's changed mixture weight is a setting revision.

E3.justification: The reported NNPE mixture weight changes from rho = 0.5 in v1 Appendix D to rho = 1 in v2 Appendix F, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added protocols test four initializations, one versus ten optimization starts, bandwidth scaling and a jointly trained then frozen OUP encoder. Retained sample sizes and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands robustness analysis with initialization and restart sensitivity, kernel-bandwidth sensitivity, learned versus fixed summary evaluation on OUP, and SIR contamination through complete trajectory distortion. Appendix B also extends the KL-versus-MMD comparison to varying contamination fractions. Earlier sample-size, dimension and detection analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 12 newly reports the standard deviation of summary distance across Gaussian-perturbed initializations. Both versions otherwise attribute plotted variability to 100 test datasets; no increase in independent training runs or new training-seed reporting is documented. Ten optimization restarts are a search-budget change.

E6.justification: Five new figures add substantive findings: initialization and restarts affect OUP accuracy, bandwidth affects performance, MDS retains advantages with a learned OUP summary and severe SIR contamination, and MMD outperforms KL adaptation across contamination fractions. All previously plotted results are retained unchanged, so these are additional findings rather than across-version performance improvements.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 replaces the fixed-outlier O(epsilon) KL statement with a supremum-over-outliers bound on infinitesimal KL change. Appendix A replaces generator-based regularity assumptions with density smoothness, integrability and nonsingularity conditions, introduces influence-function Lemma A.3 with proof, and revises the robustness proof. The consistency theorem and proof are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly scopes the introductory problem statement to Huber contamination, whereas v1 introduces model misspecification more generally. The central claims about independent query adaptation, preserved amortization, MMD robustness and posterior consistency remain.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes its infinitesimal robustness guarantee from stronger global posterior robustness. It adds explanations of initialization sensitivity, diminished influence of large-shift outliers under bounded kernels, and robustness under extensive structural SIR distortion. These qualify and extend the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds an implementation link and procedural details for the new optimization, bandwidth and learned-encoder experiments, while retaining most implementation specifications. NNPE's disclosed mixture weight changes. Algorithm 1 also introduces inconsistent observation-summation and iteration indices, reducing the reliability of its pseudocode.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges Bharti et al. (2026) as concurrent amortized, provably robust SBI and relates its robustness notion to that work. It adds Dawid and Musio, Key et al., and Newey and McFadden to support the revised theory. Most other reference changes update metadata or remove duplication.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies test-time inference and decoder explanations, edits terminology and introductory prose, and separates future work from limitations. Existing ablations and NPE-PFN material become standalone appendices before the retained experimental details. The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6, 12, 13, 25 and 28, while preserving all 25 earlier plot contents. Existing figures are relocated and renumbered, some captions are clarified, and the notation table gains a summary-statistic entry. The visual style and overall layout remain similar.

improvement.justification: The explicit robustness assumptions and local scope, new optimization and bandwidth tests, and stronger-contamination evidence make MDS easier to assess. The implementation link also improves reproducibility information. These gains outweigh limited regressions, including Algorithm 1 indexing errors and the unexplained NNPE mixture-weight revision accompanying unchanged plots.
